summary: Lung adenocarcinoma is a highly heterogeneous disease, highlighting the need for more accurate prognosis prediction. We developed a multimodal deep learning model combining preoperative computed tomography (CT) and postoperative whole slide image (WSI) to predict the disease-free survival (DFS) of resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma. Based on a cohort of 1078 patients from multiple centers, our dual-information instance neural network achieved superior performance over unimodal approaches. The risk stratification defined by the model effectively distinguished DFS in both validation cohorts and served as an independent predictor, suggesting the complementary value of the model beyond clinicopathological factors. An exploratory scoring system integrating the model-derived risk stratification with key clinicopathological factors was developed, identifying patients with significantly different prognostic outcomes. Further analyses suggested that patients with high-risk stage IB disease or high scores might derive DFS benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy, warranting prospective validation. Beyond its predictive capacity, the model also provided morphological insights, identifying prognostically significant structures such as tertiary lymphoid structures and stroma barriers, while RNA-sequencing analysis revealed distinct oncogenic pathway activation and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments in high-risk patients. By leveraging routinely acquired clinical images, this multimodal approach offers a practical tool for improving prognostic stratification, with potential implications for informing patient selection for adjuvant chemotherapy in resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma.
